questions.question: In Microsoft Fabric, lifecycle management is made up of which two capabilities?
options: Deployment pipelines and source control integration
questions.explanation: Lifecycle management in Fabric uses deployment pipelines and source control integration to achieve CI/CD.

questions.question: Which version control systems are supported for Git integration in Microsoft Fabric?
questions.explanation: GitHub and Azure DevOps are the version control systems that are supported in Fabric.

questions.question: What best describes continuous integration (CI) in a version control workflow?
options: Deploying code to production only after a formal review board approves it
Merging all finished work into the main codebase only at the end of a release cycle
Frequently committing code to a shared branch that is validated by a build process and automated testing
Automatically scaling infrastructure based on load
questions.explanation: In CI you frequently commit code to a shared branch or trunk and changes are validated by a build process and automated testing once merged.

questions.question: How does continuous deployment differ from continuous delivery?
options: Continuous deployment automatically releases updates into production through structured deployment stages once they pass automated tests
Continuous deployment only applies to source control, not pipelines
Continuous deployment requires manual approval before any release
Continuous deployment replaces version control entirely
questions.explanation: Continuous deployment automatically releases updates into production environments through structured deployment stages once they pass automated tests, whereas continuous delivery stops at a staging environment.

questions.question: At what level does Git integration operate within Microsoft Fabric?
options: At the item level for individual notebooks
questions.explanation: Integration with version control is at the workspace level in Fabric; you version items you develop within a workspace.

questions.question: In Fabric CI/CD, which component is used to implement deployment?
questions.explanation: Deployment is implemented using Fabric deployment pipelines, while integration uses Git and automation uses Fabric REST APIs.

questions.question: What is a recommended approach when combining deployment pipelines with Git integration?
options: Connect only the Development workspace to Git
Connect only the Production workspace to Git
Never use deployment pipelines with Git
Connect each pipeline stage to a separate Git repository
questions.explanation: One common approach is to connect only the Development workspace to Git, using Git for version control while deployment pipelines handle promotion to Test and Production.

questions.question: What does the Fabric CI/CD REST API 'List Deployment Pipeline Stage Items' do?
options: Deletes all items from a pipeline stage
Returns the supported items from the workspace assigned to the specified stage of a deployment pipeline
Commits changes to the connected remote branch
Updates the workspace with commits pushed to the connected branch
questions.explanation: The List Deployment Pipeline Stage Items API returns the supported items from the workspace assigned to the specified stage of the specified deployment pipeline.

questions.question: What is a best practice for keeping development work isolated from shared Fabric workspaces?
options: Working directly in the shared production workspace
Working in a dedicated branch instead of the main code branch
Disabling Git integration for all users
Creating all items in a single shared workspace
questions.explanation: Feature development work should take place in a dedicated branch instead of the main code branch, and isolated workspaces or client tools should be used.

questions.question: In Microsoft Fabric, what is monitoring?
options: The process of collecting system data and metrics that determine if a system is healthy and operating as expected
A feature that only applies to streaming data
A tool used exclusively for deploying code to production
A method for assigning licenses to users
questions.explanation: Monitoring is the process of collecting system data and metrics that determine if a system is healthy and operating as expected.

questions.question: What is the Monitor Hub in Microsoft Fabric?
options: A version control tool for Git branches
A visualization tool that aggregates activity data from selected Fabric items and processes into a common interface
A security role for granting data access
questions.explanation: Monitor hub is the monitoring visualization tool in Fabric; it collects and aggregates data from selected Fabric items and processes in one place.

questions.question: Which of the following activities can be monitored in the Monitor Hub?
questions.explanation: Monitor hub shows monitoring metadata for activities such as data pipeline execution history, dataflow executions, and Spark job execution history.

questions.question: When you select an activity in the Monitor Hub, which actions are available?
options: Opening the activity, retrying it, and viewing activity details or historical runs
Deleting the activity and its workspace
Committing the activity to a Git branch
Assigning a license to the activity owner
questions.explanation: Actions available for a selected activity vary but include options such as opening the activity, retrying it, and viewing activity details or historical runs.

questions.question: What is Activator in Microsoft Fabric?
options: A tool in Real-Time Intelligence that triggers actions on streaming data when certain conditions are met
A workspace role that grants full access
questions.explanation: Activator is a tool in Real-Time Intelligence that can be used to trigger actions on streaming data when conditions or logic are met.

questions.question: What are the four core concepts that Activator operates on?
questions.explanation: Activator operates based on four core concepts: Events, Objects, Properties, and Rules.

questions.question: In Activator, what does an Object represent?
options: The rule that triggers an action
The data in an event record used to represent a business entity such as a sales order or a sensor
A specific point in time that an event occurred
The field that maps to a property
questions.explanation: The data in an event record can be used to represent an object, such as a sales order, a sensor, or some other business entity.

questions.question: In Activator, what defines the conditions under which an action is triggered?
questions.explanation: Rules set the conditions under which an action is triggered based on the property values of objects referenced in events.

questions.question: For semantic model refreshes, what should you monitor to identify transient issues before classifying an issue as a failure?
questions.explanation: Monitor for semantic model refresh retries to help identify transient issues before classifying an issue as a failure.

questions.question: What are the three levels at which Fabric evaluates access sequentially?
options: Microsoft Entra ID authentication, Fabric access, and data security
questions.explanation: Fabric evaluates access sequentially across Microsoft Entra ID authentication, Fabric access, and data security.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four primary data security access controls?
questions.explanation: The four primary data security access controls are workspace roles, item permissions, compute or granular permissions, and OneLake security.

questions.question: Which workspace role can create, view, and modify all content and data but cannot share content or manage permissions?
questions.explanation: The Contributor role can create, view, and modify all content and data in the workspace but cannot share or manage permissions.

questions.question: What is the scope of a workspace role in Fabric?
options: A single table in a lakehouse
questions.explanation: Workspace roles apply to all items in a workspace, so assigning someone a role gives access at the level the role allows across the whole workspace.

questions.question: When you share a lakehouse, what does the Read permission always granted allow the recipient to do?
options: Read all underlying data in SQL and OneLake
See the item metadata and view associated reports, without granting access to underlying data
Assign workspace roles to other users
questions.explanation: Read permission lets the recipient see the item's metadata and view associated reports, but does not grant access to any underlying data in SQL or OneLake.

questions.question: What does the lakehouse sharing permission 'Read all Apache Spark and subscribe to events' do?
options: Grants read access through Apache Spark and OneLake APIs and adds the recipient to the DefaultReader role
Grants write access to all tables in the lakehouse
Allows the recipient to export data to Excel
Makes the recipient a workspace Admin
questions.explanation: Read all Apache Spark and subscribe to events lets a recipient read lakehouse data through Spark and OneLake APIs and also adds them to the lakehouse's DefaultReader role.

questions.question: Which Data Control Language (DCL) commands can be used to apply granular T-SQL permissions on the SQL analytics endpoint?
questions.explanation: When users query lakehouse data using T-SQL, granular permissions are applied using DCL commands GRANT, DENY, and REVOKE.

questions.question: Why is it important to remove a user from the DefaultReader role when restricting them to a custom OneLake security role?
options: DefaultReader is a workspace admin role that must always be assigned
Otherwise the user still has full read access through the default role
DefaultReader prevents users from viewing any data
Custom roles automatically add users to DefaultReader
questions.explanation: Every new lakehouse includes a DefaultReader role, so when you restrict a user to a custom role you must also remove them from DefaultReader or they retain full read access.

questions.question: Which workspace roles can create or modify OneLake security roles?
options: Only the workspace Admin and Member roles
Any user with Read item permission
questions.explanation: Only workspace Admin and Member roles can create or modify OneLake security roles.

questions.question: What is the top level of the five-level Microsoft Fabric hierarchy?
questions.explanation: The top of the Fabric hierarchy is the tenant, which represents the entire Fabric environment and aligns with the Microsoft Entra ID directory.

questions.question: Which admin role manages a specific capacity, including monitoring capacity performance?
questions.explanation: The capacity admin manages workspaces assigned to that capacity and monitors capacity performance.

questions.question: Under what name does Microsoft Entra ID list the Fabric admin role?
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra ID lists the Fabric admin role as Power BI Administrator.

questions.question: What do Fabric tenant settings control?
options: Feature availability in the UI as governance policies
Direct security access to underlying data
questions.explanation: Tenant settings control which Fabric features are available in the UI; they are governance policies, not security measures.

questions.question: Which statement about assigning a workspace to a domain is true?
options: It automatically restricts access to users in that domain
It does not change item visibility or security
It replaces workspace roles and item permissions
It moves the workspace to a different capacity
questions.explanation: Domain assignment does not change item visibility or security; domains organize governance, not access.

questions.question: What happens to Fabric workspaces that are not assigned to a capacity?
options: They fall back to shared capacity
They are assigned to the highest capacity
They run on a trial capacity
questions.explanation: Workspaces not assigned to a capacity fall back to shared capacity, which has limitations and is not suitable for production workloads.

questions.question: On an F64 or larger capacity, what license does a user need to view Power BI reports and dashboards with a viewer role?
questions.explanation: Because Contoso has an F64 capacity, users with just a Free license can view Power BI reports and dashboards if they have a viewer role on the workspace.

questions.question: Which tool contains the Feature Usage and Adoption report for tracking platform-wide usage?
questions.explanation: The admin monitoring workspace contains the Feature Usage and Adoption report and its underlying semantic model.

questions.question: Which tool does a Fabric admin use to visualize capacity unit (CU) consumption across a capacity?
options: The Microsoft Fabric Capacity Metrics app
questions.explanation: The Microsoft Fabric Capacity Metrics app lets a Fabric admin visualize CU consumption across a capacity and identify which workloads consume the most.
